title: 4 More Words That Improve Listening
author: Michael Linsin
summary: As a follow-up to the prior week's "in a moment" strategy, Linsin introduces a second phrase — "when I say go" — used just before releasing students to complete a task, meant to bridge the gap between understanding directions and executing them with speed and confidence. He instructs teachers to pause for final clarifying questions before giving the signal, since responsibility shifts entirely to students the moment "go" is said. A deliberate 15-20 second pause beforehand, he argues, causes students to mentally visualize success and builds productive suspense. Combined with the earlier "in a moment" phrase, he presents the two-part strategy as capable of turning distracted or daydreaming students into active listeners, and previews that his forthcoming book covers the broader approach in a chapter called "Shift."
points: The phrase "when I say go," said right before releasing students to a task, bridges the gap between understanding directions and executing with speed and confidence.
Pause for final clarifying questions before giving the "go" signal — once said, responsibility shifts entirely to students.
A deliberate 15-20 second pause before saying "go" causes students to mentally visualize success, building useful suspense.
Combined with the earlier "in a moment" phrase, the two-part strategy is meant to turn distracted or daydreaming students into active listeners.
quotes: The phrase “in a moment” keeps students from moving on while you’re giving directions.
It bridges the gap between knowing what to do and doing it with speed, accuracy, and confidence.
Because once you say ‘go,’ you’re handing responsibility in total over to them—with very reluctant additional support from you.
A final pause of 15-20 seconds will cause students to visualize themselves successfully doing whatever you want them to do.
This simple two-part strategy of giving directions— in a moment and when I say go —can turn distracted, bored, and daydreaming students into active and tenacious listeners.
